public.title: Spreadsheet II
public.description: input {cells,queries}; cells map names to integer constants or formula token arrays [operand,operator,operand,...]. An operand is an integer or cell-name string, operators are +, - and *. Evaluate every formula strictly left to right, ignoring usual multiplication precedence; resolve referenced formulas recursively, missing cells as 0. The graph is acyclic, depth at most 4, at most 3 operators/formula, at most 12 cells and 20 queries. Return one integer per queried name; every intermediate result is within 1000000 in absolute value. Supported inputs are valid for this contract. Aggregate JSON-serialized input is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, nesting depth at most 6, arrays at most 40 items, operation/call lists at most 20 items, and individual strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless a tighter bound is stated. Integers have absolute value at most 1000; output arithmetic stays within safe integers. String object keys and string path segments are nonempty safe alphanumeric/underscore names excluding __proto__, constructor and prototype. Empty arrays/objects are allowed where consistent with the contract. Output ordering follows the rules above. These bounds include all nested payloads and all operations together.
hints: Separate the documented JSON representation from the behavior being modeled.
Preserve ordering and distinguish missing values, null, zero and false carefully.

explanation: Recursively resolve operands then fold each formula from left to right. With b operands and dependency depth h, time per query is O(b to the h), stack O(h); the bounded grammar keeps work small. Functional tests check the documented adapter behavior; they do not enforce implementation technique or prohibit built-in APIs.
